purpose: Verify the pressure-head derivative-difference observer against exact temporal error on a linear semi-discrete Richards eigenmode whose state dependence is carried only by the existing mixed storage and Darcy operator.

manufactured_hydraulics.top_boundary: explicit qtop=-K so the gravity component cancels at the top
manufactured_hydraulics.bottom_boundary: SWBOTB=5 with hbot=h_eq so the gravity component cancels and perturbation has homogeneous Dirichlet condition

semi_discrete_perturbation_system.runtime_precheck: A*v=lambda*M*v must hold to a machine-epsilon-scaled algebraic consistency bound before any solver result is interpreted

pass_rules: The generalized eigenpair precheck passes before HeadCalc execution.
All five HeadCalc solves converge with max_iterations=8, max_backtracking=4 and unchanged 1e-12 numerical balance controls.
Each computed HeadCalc endpoint agrees with the analytic backward-Euler eigenmode endpoint under an epsilon-scaled numerical-consistency bound only.
Each computed e_h agrees with the analytic derivative-difference expression under an epsilon-scaled numerical-consistency bound only.
The discrete water ledger closes from storage change plus top/bottom boundary exchange; no source/sink term exists.
The exact manufactured continuous water accounting is consistent with boundary exchange implied by the exact eigenmode; no water is created or discarded in the manufactured definition.
rho>1 for all five frozen lambda*dt values and decreases strictly at every refinement.
maxabs(e_h) and maxabs(err_exact) each decrease strictly at every refinement.
O0 and O2 machine-readable outputs are identical.
Production Richards/runtime source remains identical to the F-VQ29 base.

can_qualify: observer implementation algebra on an exact state-dependent HeadCalc hydraulic problem
conservative asymptotic relation on this manufactured eigenmode
compatibility with unchanged mass-conservative backward-Euler principal advancement
cannot_qualify: rho>=1 on nonlinear B1.10 soil hydraulics

next_if_pass: Freeze Gate C2 physical-envelope transfer characterization using real B1.10 constitutive hydraulics and finite same-endpoint evidence only as finite evidence, never as exact truth.
